summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of liver transplant, diabetes, and recent hernia repair was admitted for evaluation of fevers and chills at home. He was found to have hyperkalemia and acute kidney injury on chronic kidney disease, likely prerenal in origin due to reduced intake during illness. He was treated with kayexalate and IV fluids, with improvement in potassium and renal function. Infectious workup was negative, including normal chest X-ray, negative C. diff toxin, and no growth in urine culture; blood cultures later identified Enterobacter cloacae complex but were interpreted in the context of likely contamination. The fever resolved without antibiotics, presumed viral. Tacrolimus was discontinued and sirolimus increased to 4 mg daily given therapeutic levels and concern for tacrolimus-related nephrotoxicity. Lasix was held during admission. The patient was discharged home afebrile with follow-up arranged in the transplant clinic and instructions to monitor sirolimus levels.
problems: Diabetes mellitus without mention of complication, type II or unspecified type, uncontrolled
Diaphragmatic hernia without mention of obstruction or gangrene
Hypertensive chronic kidney disease, unspecified, with chronic kidney disease stage I through stage IV, or unspecified
